gloss: carefree; having known no hardship; sheltered

definitions.gloss: carefree; having known no hardship; sheltered; inexperienced in difficulty
definitions.explanation: Describing someone who has grown up or lived without ever experiencing real struggle or hardship, often implying a privileged or sheltered upbringing.

examples.japanese: {苦労知|くろうし}らず⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{育|そだ}った→育つ：01951_sodatsu⟧。
examples.english: I grew up without knowing hardship.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{苦労知|くろうし}らず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧お{坊|ぼっ}ちゃんだ。
examples.english: He is a sheltered rich kid who has never known hardship.

examples.japanese: {苦労知|くろうし}らずだった⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{社会|しゃかい}→社会：01427_shakai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|で}て→出る：00513_deru⟧⟦{初|はじ}めて→初めて：02932_hajimete⟧⟦{大変|たいへん}→大変：00594_taihen⟧さ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{知|し}った→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: Having been sheltered, I learned for the first time how tough things are when I entered the real world.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{苦労|くろう}→苦労：02672_kurou⟧ (hardship, difficulty) and ⟦{知|し}ら→知る：00458_shiru⟧ず (not knowing). Describes someone who has been fortunate enough — or sheltered enough — to never experience real difficulty. The tone can be neutral (simply describing someone's fortunate upbringing) or slightly critical (implying naivety or a lack of empathy due to inexperience).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {苦労知|くろうし}らず⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{育|そだ}つ→育つ：01951_sodatsu⟧: to grow up without hardship
- {苦労知|くろうし}らず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人生|じんせい}→人生：03355_jinsei⟧: a life without hardship
- {苦労知|くろうし}らず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧お{坊|ぼっ}ちゃん: sheltered rich boy

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{世間知|せけんし}らず→世間知らず：22674_sekenshirazu⟧: naive about the ways of the world — focuses on social inexperience
- のんき: carefree, easygoing — personality trait rather than life circumstance
- お⟦{気楽|きらく}→気楽：07159_kiraku⟧: carefree, happy-go-lucky — more colloquial and often slightly critical
